clue.text: Pressure after vote in nearby country's become invalid

indicators.note: the vote-and-pressure pair is set inside the name of the neighbouring country

parts.note: Eire, the Irish name for Ireland, is Britain's near neighbour

indicators.note: the pressure letter is placed after the voting mark

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A political crisis abroad: a vote under pressure in a neighbouring country leaves something null and void.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence or passport that runs out ceases to be valid, so lapsing is becoming invalid.

clue.text: Prohibit European doctor going on legendary vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue the ship's name is attached after the doctor, continuing the chain

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A European medic boarding a mythical ship, as though someone wants to stop them sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade is an embargo, so to impose one is to prohibit.

clue.text: Right-winger in US, type that's irritating about left

indicators.note: the irritating type goes around the letter for left

parts.note: an annoying person is called a pain

explanation.surface: A jibe at an American conservative as a tiresome person who goes on about the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin is a Republican politician, former governor of Alaska and 2008 vice-presidential candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Palin, the Alaskan Republican, is a well-known conservative politician in America.

clue.text: Not acting on trap set up by police

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a sting is an undercover operation to catch criminals

explanation.surface: Someone reporting on a police entrapment operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not acting' reads as inactive, but it is the theatre sense: an actor out of work is said to be resting.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre euphemism: an unemployed actor between roles is politely described as resting.

clue.text: Puts on in revised version that's clear

indicators.note: a revised version rearranges what came before, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a new edition that is easier to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To unstop a drain or pipe is to clear the blockage from it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Drama with extinct bird, mostly about having ceased to be

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is classical Japanese theatre

indicators.note: most of the bird's name is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, hunted to extinction
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A play about an extinct bird, echoing the Monty Python dead parrot sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes Monty Python's Dead Parrot sketch ('This parrot is no more! It has ceased to be!'), which also lies behind 26 and 27 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that exists no longer has ceased to be; the phrase is the sketch's own wording.

clue.text: Para unit deployed around line to provide protection for sailor

indicators.note: the rearranged paratroop letters go round the line letter
troops deployed are spread out into new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paratroops spread out to give cover to a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide protection for' leads to the familiar sense, a waterproof sheet, but the definition is the old one: a tarpaulin, or tar, was a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin was an old nickname for a seaman, from the tarred canvas hats and clothes they wore; 'tar' is short for it.

clue.text: Pair with a bit of script that's nutty stuff

parts.note: a line is a single part of an actor's script

explanation.surface: Two actors sharing a line from a script, with an odd hint of something crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Praline is a confection of nuts cooked in sugar, hence a nut-based sweet.

clue.text: Property of sheep and goats in story, in different senses

indicators.note: the story sits inside the rearranged letters
made different, the letters of senses are rearranged

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral, like those in the Gospels

explanation.surface: A biblical story about sheep and goats, read in several senses.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew's Gospel the parable of the sheep and the goats has them divided at the Last Judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep and goats can be told apart and divided, so their quality is the capacity to be parted.

clue.text: Name the first to be knocked off

definitions.text: Name the first to be knocked off

indicators.text: the first to be knocked off
indicators.note: the opening letter of the naming word is removed

parts.note: a label names something

explanation.surface: An instruction to identify who was killed first.
explanation.walkthrough: Abel, killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, was the first murder victim: the whole clue defines him while also giving the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel is slain by Cain, the first person ever murdered.

clue.text: Powerful instrument included in contents of chest buried in South by pirate

indicators.note: the chest's contents are put inside the pair of south and the pirate

parts.note: Sir Henry Morgan was a notorious Welsh buccaneer of the Caribbean
a tea chest holds tea

explanation.surface: A pirate burying a chest of treasure in the south, with a big instrument inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The pirate's chest suggests buried treasure, but it is a tea chest; 'buried in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam organ, or calliope, is a loud fairground instrument driven by steam power.

clue.text: Land in East, namely, taken back after British period

indicators.note: the turned-round namely letters follow British and period

parts.note: a run is a spell or period, as in a run of luck

indicators.note: taken back means the abbreviation is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: i.e., id est, means namely

explanation.surface: A territory in the East reclaimed after a spell of British rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Roman emperor's endless automatic action in waters off Italy

indicators.note: the emperor's name loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: Hadrian was the Roman emperor who built the wall across northern England
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: An emperor's ceaseless reflexive movements in the sea near Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adriatic Sea lies between Italy's east coast and the Balkans.

clue.text: New organ I ordered from country in Europe

indicators.note: an instrument ordered from abroad, but here the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a new church organ from a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from Norway, a Scandinavian nation, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Certainly knowing setter and solver exist without barrier being put up

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the pair encloses the barrier

parts.note: the setter and the solver together are we
are means exist, as in 'we are'

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written bottom to top, so the barrier is turned round

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Setter and solver are fully conscious of each other with nothing between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'put up' reverses the barrier because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fully informed about something means knowing it for sure, an idiomatic intensified awareness.

clue.text: Sportsman needing to be cheered

definitions.meaning: at Oxford and Cambridge a ... is someone who has represented the university in a sport
feeling sad or down, needing cheering up

explanation.walkthrough: A blue is an Oxford or Cambridge athlete who has competed against the other university.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a university sporting honour and its holder, and the colour's sense of melancholy.

clue.text: Has a complaint and is lambasting shopkeeper up front

indicators.note: only the front letter of each of these four words is used

explanation.surface: A disgruntled customer complains and lays into a shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unwell or troubled is to have a complaint, in the medical sense of an ailment.

clue.text: Doesn't put in prison, even under a Conservative

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for even sits below the other two pieces

parts.note: being quits means being even, with nothing owed

explanation.surface: A Tory government that keeps people out of jail, settling scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that clears a defendant finds them not guilty, so frees rather than jails them.

clue.text: Look for bill with extra length — characteristic of a healthy bird?

indicators.note: the length letter is added inside the searching word

parts.note: to seek is to look for
a bill is a headland, like Portland Bill; ness is another word for one

explanation.surface: Looking at a bird's beak with extra length as a sign of good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' wants to be a beak, but here it is a promontory: NESS, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness, a headland in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-fed bird has glossy, smooth plumage; that glossy smoothness is what the clue describes, with a question mark.

clue.text: Oddly, it's a volcano — even so, I land in northern Europe

indicators.note: oddly signals the volcano's letters take the odd-numbered places, rearranging the pieces together

parts.note: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling travel note: a volcano, yet a Baltic country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' and 'even' work together: ETNA fills the odd positions (1, 3, 5, 7) and S, O, I fill the even ones, giving E-S-T-O-N-I-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea, in northern Europe.

clue.text: Revised atlases showing result of oceanic evaporation

indicators.note: a revised book is redone, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: New editions of maps showing where seawater dries off.
explanation.definitionFit: When seawater dries up it leaves behind crystals of salt, harvested for cooking.

clue.text: Intended to arouse emotion — result, initially, of hearing organ

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words before it are used

parts.note: otic is the technical adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: Sound affecting the feelings through the ear, almost a scientific definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexually suggestive material is designed to stimulate desire, which is to arouse.

clue.text: Second question changed around for operational unit

indicators.note: changed tells us these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A moment's query turning a unit round.
explanation.definitionFit: An air force or naval squadron is a working military unit of aircraft or ships.

clue.text: Dreadful cut on a bird with beautiful plumage

indicators.note: a dreadful mess is a jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty wound on a gorgeous tropical bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a South American bird with a huge colourful bill and bright plumage.

clue.text: Concluding you can find the answer below

indicators.note: only the closing letter of each word that follows is used

explanation.surface: A solving instruction: the answer is lower down the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath and beneath are synonyms, and this word means beneath.

clue.text: Major cut to obsolete weapon, with political co-operation

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: big means major or large
a partisan was a medieval spear with a broad blade

explanation.surface: A big reduction in old armaments, agreed across party lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like John Major, the former Prime Minister, but it is just big.
explanation.definitionFit: Policies backed by both parties involve cross-party agreement, the parties working together.

clue.text: Having lately joined a certain choir? Absolutely

definitions.text: Having lately joined a certain choir?
definitions.meaning: the 'choir invisible' is a poetic phrase for the departed, so newly joining it means having passed away
as in ... right or ... certain, completely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joined the choir invisible' is one of the euphemisms for death in Monty Python's Dead Parrot sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: deceased, and the adverb meaning completely, as in dead on time.

clue.text: Outline of small boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A rough drawing of a little vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dead Parrot sketch is the theme: this answer names the form it takes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough preliminary drawing gives the outline of something, as does a brief summary.

clue.text: Character holding rook and duck — or another bird

indicators.note: the character word holds the two pieces inside it

parts.note: an actor's part is the character played
R is the chess notation for rook
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, hence O

explanation.surface: A figure holding a crow and a duck, then a third bird for good measure.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket, so it stands for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a bird, the third after rook and duck in the clue, and the Python sketch's subject.
